As anticipated here we have completed a formalization of the Hadamard factorization theorem (here) and of its application to the riemannZeta (here). Since the Hadamard factorization is supposed to play a key role in the formalization of the third path to PNT in PNT+ we thought it may be of interest that we have now refactored it to be more Mathlib/PNT+ idiomatic and self-contained, and we would be glad to PR it to PNT+.
We have tried to follow closely the main proof step and statement given by Terence Tao here (and we hav tried to leverage PNT+ and StrongPNT API as much as we could, though certainly a deeper integration could be achieved) to ensure the API could match the expectations in PNT+.
We haven’t directly PR’d the code to the main repository yet, since the very recent official contribution guidelines formally require contribution on open issues or tasks, but we are happy to proceed as you deem it fit, including connecting the code to the blueprint and doing additional refactor or golfing of the lengthier proofs, as well as helping porting idiomatically the parts of StrongPNT used.
However we have PR’d it to this fork of PNT+, ready to be upstreamed to main if, as and when deemed appropriate by @Alex Kontorovich and @Terence Tao .
In this refactor we have removed the ZeroData structure (useful but not mathlib idiomatic) so that the final theorem takes intrinsic hypotheses on an entire function f, e.g. EntireOfFiniteOrder ρ f, and do not require a user-supplied ZeroData. The proof now internally obtains an enumeration of zeros (or an appropriate divisor) and then applies canonical product API developed in the WeierstarssFactor, CanonicalProduct, Divisor, LogSingularity, CartanBound, ExpPoly and the main files.

There are prerequisites that we aim to submit to Mathlib soon and that we have temporarily added them to the Mathlib folder. They also include 2 files from Carleson that we have used to avoid reduplicating API for Annuli and which seem to be meant to be upstreamed to Mathlib at some point.
Upstreaming the application of this refactored version of Hadamard factorization to the zeta function would require an additional set of prerequisites involving the Gamma function and Stirling bounds that we have also added in the Mathlib folder, to which we would need to add some extracts from StrongPNT.Complex; as they would be too much to swallow in one cycle the zeta corollaries are probably better suited for a subsequent cycle of PRs.

This looks great! Definitely this factorization will be useful later in the explicit PNT project. I haven't been as involved with StrongPNT, so I'll let Alex speak to how it would fit in there, but assuming it is compatible, I for one would be happy to have it PR'ed.

Indeed this is great! Since we already have Borel-Caratheodory, we no longer "need" Hadamard, but of course it would be good to have in general, and I'd be very happy if you decided to upstream it to PNT+. (I suppose even better, as long as you're upstreaming, would be to upstream to Mathlib, so that PNT+ gets it automatically at the next bump. But maybe it's a big file and not Mathlib-ready, in which case, we'd be happy to help host it!)

I've been looking at Kadiri's approach to establishing classical zero-free regions for the Riemann zeta function and it turns out that her method uses the Hadamard factorization of the Riemann xi function. So now would be a good time to push the PR of HadamardFactorization.lean; I take it that only some precursors are in Mathlib right now?

Specifically, Kadiri uses the identity
−ζ′(s)ζ(s)=−B−12log⁡π+1s−1+12Γ′Γ(s2+1)−∑ρ1ρ+1s−ρ -\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)} = - B - \frac{1}{2} \log \pi + \frac{1}{s-1} + \frac{1}{2} \frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{s}{2}+1) - \sum_\rho \frac{1}{\rho} + \frac{1}{s-\rho}−ζ(s)ζ′(s)​=−B−21​logπ+s−11​+21​ΓΓ′​(2s​+1)−∑ρ​ρ1​+s−ρ1​
where ρ\rhoρ ranges over non-trivial zeroes and B=ξ′(0)ξ(0) B = \frac{\xi'(0)}{\xi(0)}B=ξ(0)ξ′(0)​. She also needs ReB=−∑ρRe1ρ \mathrm{Re} B =- \sum_\rho \mathrm{Re} \frac{1}{\rho}ReB=−∑ρ​Reρ1​ but this follows relatively easily from the functional equation ξ(s)=ξ(1−s)\xi(s) = \xi(1-s)ξ(s)=ξ(1−s) after taking log-derivatives at s=1s=1s=1.

Can you please point me to where that is? I wonder if the use of Hadamard here can be replaced by Borel-Caratheodory, which we now have in PNT+ (and possibly also already in Mathlib). [But then we're changing the proof in the paper, which is maybe not the point of the project?]

Oh, I'm sorry, I forgot to supply links. The identity is used on page 13 of https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0401238 . Kadiri's approach is to get an explicit formula for Re∑nΛ(n)nsf(log⁡n)(1−κnδ)\mathrm{Re} \sum_n \frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^s} f(\log n) (1 - \frac{\kappa}{n^\delta})Re∑n​nsΛ(n)​f(logn)(1−nδκ​) for reasonably smooth, compactly supported fff in terms of zeroes and some gamma factors, and some real parameters κ,δ\kappa,\deltaκ,δ to be numerically optimized later. This is applied to s=σ+ikγ0s = \sigma + i k\gamma_0s=σ+ikγ0​ where σ0+iγ0\sigma_0+i\gamma_0σ0​+iγ0​ is a putative zero of zeta close to the edge Res=1\mathrm{Re} s = 1Res=1 for various small integer kkk, and a weighted sum is then taken (a la Mertens) to make the sum non-negative; but if σ0\sigma_0σ0​ is reasonably close to 111 one can make the right-hand side of the identity negative, giving a contradiction. (Amusingly, there is an iterative aspect to the approach, namely that in order to control the error term involving sums over zeroes, an existing zero-free region is needed.)

Without the full Hadamard identity one could create truncated versions of this identity (particularly if we changed the cutoff fff to be compactly supported in Fourier space rather than in physical space), but this creates more error terms and moves one away from the literature. If the Hadamard factorization theorem is essentially ready to be imported into PNT then I'd say we just establish the Hadamard identity, it is a pretty standard fact and opens the door to all the other completely explicit formulae involving the von Mangoldt function.

Hadamard went through a substantial (though unfinished) refactor in this mathlib branch. It follows closely Tao's notes here. One mathlib PR is currently open and I'm planning to continue in small pieces.
However since that will take long I'd be happy to upstream it to PNT+ and maintain the code. I'll try to open the first PRs asap

Since Matteo's Hadamard work is intended to provide the completed zeta factor / ξ\xiξ factorization-log-derivative input, it seemed useful to provide a Kadiri-facing bridge turning that input into the explicit −ζ′/ζ-\zeta'/\zeta−ζ′/ζ identity.

I opened a PR here

The main theorem is Kadiri.neg_zeta_logDeriv_eq_of_genusOne_hadamard

It packages the implication logDeriv completedZetaFactor s =  B + genusOneZeroLogSum zero s into the classical Kadiri formula for −ζ′/ζ-\zeta'/\zeta−ζ′/ζ, adding the pole, gamma, π\piπ, and Hadamard zero-sum terms.

The PR also contains a centered Hadamard zero-orbit variant together with the finite cancellation

E₁(w/α) * E₁(w/(-α)) = 1 - w^2/α^2

which seemed like a useful small algebraic layer for a possible functional-equation/orbit formulation. Happy to adjust the API if this looks useful for the Hadamard/Kadiri direction.
